doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: His Lebanese parents and Hardine
summary: Grandparents came from Lebanon, from the town Hardine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I neglected to ask you about your own parents.

They were here, their parents came from Lebanon and of course they came from a small town named Hardine, which no one ever heard of, until I got to Syracuse. I met a doctor who treated my wife when she was getting evaluated for cancer. Of course she was just getting evaluated at the time. And he said, “Oh yeah,” he says, “I’ve heard of Hardine,” he says, “I’ve been there.” He says, “Your wife’s not Lebanese,” he says, “you are” he says, “I hear you speak the language.” I says, “I only know the names of the food” I says, © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-
“I don’t speak the language.” He says, “Well you mentioned that in one word” he says, “you’re from Hardine,” he says, “they’re the only people that pronounce it that way.
